factor_ratings.evidence: Manages a 4-person RTL sub-team on one block (digital front-end of NX-400); impact contained to that sub-team and the block, not the function
Owns sprint planning and code review sign-off for the group, and sets own approach on the clock/reset RTL block, but scope is a single sub-team, not an area spanning multiple teams
Still personally solving ambiguous RTL design problems on clock/reset architecture; managerial complexity is limited to running one small sub-team's process
Deep in RTL/digital design discipline, personally owns clock/reset architecture; no evidence of cross-disciplinary breadth
Owns a subsystem (clock/reset RTL) across a development cycle -- factor 5a L4 anchor; no evidence of platform or multi-generation architecture ownership
Influence limited to the sub-team and sign-off authority within it; no evidence of cross-functional or executive influence described
4 direct reports, all individual contributors, no budget authority beyond headcount requisitions -- matches M3 anchor exactly

decision.governing_rule: Manager level from scope of impact and span & budget corroboration (section 4, span & budget table); rule 6 -- title 'Senior MTS' is evidence, not input
decision.alternative_reasoning: Considered M4 given the 'Senior' title modifier and performance-review authority, but rejected: span (4 ICs) falls well below the M4 anchor (10-25, may include a team lead), there is no program budget, and scope of impact is confined to a single sub-team/block rather than spanning multiple teams -- rule 5 explicitly warns manager level is not automatic from headcount or title, and rule 6 requires leveling from described scope, not title.
decision.escalation_factor: scope_of_impact -- if the NX-400 digital front-end sub-team's work is shown to shape decisions across multiple teams/blocks rather than being contained to this one block, M4 would be indicated
decision.reasoning: Despite the 'Senior' modifier in the title, the described scope is a first-line manager of a 4-person IC sub-team with no budget authority beyond requisitions -- this matches the M3 anchor exactly (4-10 direct reports, all ICs, no budget authority beyond requisitions). Scope of impact is contained to a single sub-team/block, not spanning multiple teams or the function, which would be required for M4. The individual continuing to personally own the clock/reset RTL block is itself L4-level IC work (owns a subsystem across a full development cycle per factor 5a), reinforcing M3 (M3's IC equivalent is L4). All non-span factors point to L4-equivalent scope, and span & budget confirms M3. No factor indicates M4 (which requires 10-25 people, a program budget, or impact across the function). Source org context: whole company, 104 headcount (small/growth-adjacent), org_depth 4, low platform dependency. Small-company titles are expected to map down 1-2 levels per section 6 -- 'Senior MTS, Engineering Manager' mapping to M3 is consistent with this prior, raising confidence rather than contradicting it.
